explicit_debrief_messages.text: My NG/MJ preference survived the game and gained evidence: Guild authority performed its repair duty, and both Security delegates agreed useful operations. The package passed eight of eleven despite both army refusals. That is an imposed settlement on the Janissariat, not consensus; I accepted the imbalance rather than sacrifice commercial independence. GS mattered: they checked Vigil against duplicate Warrant use, insisted that next month's Repair be funded, and independently refused MA while preserving our separate Lantern pledge. Trade and Maintain were credible unilateral alternatives, so withholding Wayfarer was a real bargaining position. We conceded tender service and accepted a temporary beacon deficit; the army conceded conditioning and the crown spent its reserve. In round one the disclosure left my assets unchanged but changed requested orders from Hold/Guard to reserve Relief and Raid/Warrant, with a repair bargain. In round two it changed only knowledge and confidence: Repair/Trade already qualified for the reported benefit. Public drafts helped expose the transport disagreement before purchase and made those different effects visible. The Lantern lock constrained later choice by our own consent. I suggest putting the reserve's lodged task alongside final asset sheets: I had to request its confirmation. This one play cannot establish that disclosure caused the good ending, and I do not know either unbought answer.

I judged upkeep and civilian scrutiny worth that disagreement. GN's specific contribution was turning the Beacon-one compromise into a funded Repair plan and Lantern pledge, preserving our second contract. It made the trade-linked target intelligible and strengthened bargaining for funded compensation; written reserve confirmation increased confidence before r1_orders_GS.

Displayed drafts helped distinguish that reassurance from an actual change of plan; the locked Lantern pledge constrained reassignment, not the vision purchase itself.

Our temporary tender commitment and upkeep duty were real concessions; the crown spent reserve and foresight, and the army accepted conditioning decline. Independent trade remained credible. I considered Interim preferable to MA and MI a possible final fallback. The outcome cannot prove either purchase was necessary, and I never learned the unbought answers.

We preserved Spear and finished at readiness three with full communities, but lost our constitutional argument. NG/MJ passed eight of eleven despite both army refusals. I accepted Guild discretion after its repair undertaking; I never accepted unequal scrutiny as the price of service. JS made our counteroffer concrete by proposing Vigil Home attached to MA, and later agreed to protection despite MA's rejection. We conceded conditioning and voluntarily offered Vigil; independent Raid remained possible but uncertain and costly under Interim.

Round one disclosure changed my requests from Military/Campaign to Relief/Raid while Council assignments stayed fixed. The completed-Trade condition made the local fight credible; the reserve offer made its civilian cost acceptable. Those arrived together, so I cannot isolate information from that material bargain. Round two disclosure raised confidence in Repair/Trade and the noncombat outcome. My switch from Restraint plus Warrant to Guard without Warrant coordinated with the crown's plan; the supply benefit did not mechanically require that switch or establish a Raid target.

Drafts before purchase helped expose our first-round transport mismatch and distinguish the second-round protection wording from its shared purpose. They also gave clear records of what actually changed. I know neither unbought answer.

explicit_debrief_messages.text: NG/MJ passed with eight of eleven leverage despite both our refusals. The physical outcome is strong, but our institution accepted restraint and protection without securing autonomy or reciprocal control of passage. I accepted the Guild's delivered Repair as evidence for NG; I did not accept it as grounds for its military veto. JN made the autonomy offer concrete through T2's Vigil pledge, then proposed reciprocal NJ/MJ, giving our objection an alternative. Independent Raid was a real option, weakened by discipline costs, civilian losses and uncertain targets; withholding Vigil was possible but would have damaged communities for little gain. Round one's disclosure left my assignments unchanged but changed Military/Campaign requests to Relief/Raid, with completed Trade, reserve Relief and Warrant making that bargain credible. Round two's distribution disclosure improved confidence in repair and commerce; changing Restraint/Warrant to Guard/no Warrant coordinated protection rather than revealing a combat opportunity. I never learned that round's Raid answer. Displaying drafts first exposed the missing passage and focused the first purchase on a live alternative. The sequence helped me distinguish the plan from the information; it does not prove what we would have chosen without it.

explicit_debrief_messages.text:
NG/MJ passed with eight of eleven leverage despite both military refusals. I retain my judgment that it can work, but their objection to unequal institutional concessions remains unresolved. Guild repair under delegated authority and both Security delegates' actual agreements justified surrendering my command. The Guild supplied Lantern and upheld upkeep; the army offered both assets, guarded communities and accepted conditioning decline. Civilians paid the Raid's costs; I spent Grey Petrel and two foresight tokens.

Round one: Guild Trade drafts blocked my proposed Campaign, making the Security cover's Raid question immediately relevant. I bought R1-S and changed Military/Campaign to reserve Relief/council Raid, retaining Warrant. Its target condition enabled a concrete compromise. Losing one leverage point was justified by that operational use.

Round two: both Guild drafts paired Repair with Trade, exactly within R2-N's scope. I bought it to understand civilian supplies while Guard and Restraint were discussed. My Repair/Guard/no-Warrant draft did not change. The distribution information improved confidence and our accounting, rather than changing my orders. In retrospect its leverage cost bought less practical value; declining would have been defensible, although I did not know the answer beforehand.

I chose no NONE option. One token remained because only two purchases were allowed, not because I deliberately saved one. Next test: add one operational round under the ratified constitution to observe whether military dissent affects offers and whether joint Security can sustain cooperation without my intervention.
